claim: What one new line completes, for the creation map (knots of up to three points, the four census far sides). (1) The two-bit screening lemma: an intact Fano side standing in for a line acts as that line for creation; the new knots off it are the closed space's, and a new knot through it occurs only where the closed space has one. (2) The splitting lemma for both kinds of atom: an intact Fano atom, attached at a point or at a line, can be contracted to its element without changing creation outside it. (3) In spaces built from Fano atoms alone, a line creates at another exactly when it does in the chain of their atoms. (4) The touching rule at distances up to two: in every such space, a line creates at a line of another atom at most two atoms away exactly when that line touches its atom's cut toward the first, and lines of one atom are mutual; so the brace dictionary up to distance two is a theorem and every cut is read in its direction. What remains for the source rule is a transfer along chains of four or more atoms.
